name: Vampiric Undead
background:
The Vampiric Undead are legions of monsters and their mortal servants led by powerful vampire Lords. These lords use their dark magic to raise the dead, and lead them to battle alongside their mortal servants. 

The Vampire Lords are members of the nobility from the western steppes who embraced necromancy after they were abandoned by the Empire during the Havoc Wars. Once they understood the secret of immortality, they attempted to betray their patrons and were cursed with undeath. This curse has only made the Vampire Lords more bitter and cruel as they rule brutally over their fearful subjects.
backgroundFull:
The Vampiric Undead originate from the western reaches of the Empire. Their lands were divided into a handful of counties made up of small villages scattered over the Western Steppes, beyond the Dwarven Mountains. Far from the centre of the Old Empire, these lands were undeveloped and often overlooked, raided by nomadic Ogres and other neighbours. 

When the Havoc Wars began, most of the armies and nobility of the Steppes were summoned, along with the rest of the Imperial vassals, to defend the Empire’s northern borders. The Steppe was left largely unguarded, and it was soon overrun by marauding neighbours and outlaws. Desperate to defend their lands, the remaining nobles began to listen to the promises of an exiled wizard, known as the Great Necromancer. This wizard offered these nobles the armies that they needed, in exchange for an oath of loyalty to his mysterious patrons. Those nobles who accepted his offer would see their enemies driven out and their graveyards emptied, as the wizard raised the dead to fight. 

The Great Necromancer introduced the nobles to his patrons, strange and lifeless beings from another plane. These patrons offered the nobility the secret of immortality if the nobles would give them a piece of Tyria to live in. The nobles eagerly accepted the pact and began using their undead armies to conquer their neighbours to carve out a new realm. Yet, when the time came to complete the deal, they betrayed the wizard and his patrons, severing the link between the planes, and stealing the knowledge for themselves. 

They eagerly attempted the ritual, sacrificing the wizard in the process. However, the ritual did not result in their immortality, but instead turned them into the first generation of Tyrian Vampires. The Vampiric Nobles, lacking a clear leader, shifted the blame on each other for the ritual’s failure, and soon fought for dominance over the rest. These Vampires viewed their mortal subjects as mere cattle, useful only as nourishment and a means to create more undead. 

When the Rift opened, some whispered that the Great Necromancer’s old patrons had returned, seeking revenge. Meanwhile, from the east, one of the Emperor’s own children arrived in the steppes as an undead immortal. Desperate and weary of their endless internal conflicts, many Vampires have submitted to him, hoping that they might unite together to protect themselves and expand their realms once more. 

How will you harness your power over death itself?

product.description: Among the indifferent ranks of Skeletons, who move at a uniform pace, bound by the spells that raised them, Skeleton Champions stand out. Beyond the stark blackness of their orbits, there seems to be a glimmer of individuality. When their skull suddenly turns to face a particular enemy, and they raise their weapon to issue a challenge, it is as shocking as seeing a puppet suddenly ignore its strings.

Few Vampiric Undead armies take to the field without at least one Necromancer; they are Humans who have learnt the secrets of the Curse and can use its energy to cast spells and raise the dead. Contrary to Vampires, they have not been physically changed by the Curse, except for being able to prolong their lives beyond their natural years. Lacking the Vampires’ raw power, Necromancers focus on supporting their army by using their arcane knowledge to reinforce units, either by granting them additional strength and quickness or by summoning reinforcements to replenish thinning ranks.

Vampire Lords are dangerous adversaries. Despite their Human-like appearance, they are infused with the wretched energy of the Curse, which confers them strength and vigour far beyond those of mere mortals, as well as innate arcane powers that some of them have used to master the dark art of necromancy. Doomed to forever suffer from an inextinguishable thirst for blood, Vampire Lords unleash their repressed urges on the battlefield, turning them into ferocious fighters that will stop at nothing to strike down their opponents.

Latmyir the Mad is a powerful necromancer obsessed with perfecting the art of raising Skeletons. He was one of the earliest apprentices of the Stranger. Some have said that the Curse drove him mad, while others insist he was exactly the same before. In order to capture more of the warrior’s souls, Latmyir conducts experiments with long burials accompanied with varied rituals. He keeps running into the problem that most of the souls he drags back into their skeletons react very poorly to it. His enemies are terrified by tales of him trapping his enemy’s souls into inanimate objects.

Ekvanyik “Blackfang” Tsaveskoz, an infamous Vampire adventurer, started as the Knight-Commander of the port town of Grazye. Unsatisfied with his low place in the ranks of Vampire Nobility, Tsaveskoz sought to make a name for himself, and decided to find outside of the Marches the glory that he couldn’t attain in his homeland.  Before he even took the name Blackfang, Knight-Commander Tsaveskoz was known for his greed. He had been a fearsome warrior in his mortal days, ruthlessly cutting down Havoc Warriors with his cutlass.

Ghoul Champions are the smartest and strongest of their kin. Even grizzled veterans can find themselves shaking in fear when they see a snarling creature leap at them, its toxin claws dripping with venom, its wounds seemingly healing in mere minutes. Where most Ghouls are unable to express themselves beyond unnerving groans and yelps, Champions can somewhat communicate with other species. And while they look just as horrifying as their brethren, they can be deceivingly intelligent, on par with any elegant Vampire.

The love story between Navleva and her husband Count Grevrig is one of the great romances of the Marches; many songs have been written about their story, from its heartwarming start to its tragic ending. Navleva was born in a Human town close to Verdorv. The Count fell in love with her at first sight and so did she. After several years of marriage, she asked him to make her a Vampire so that they could spend eternity together. Like her husband, the Countess became a fervent proponent of undead-mortal cohabitation and maintained a large correspondence with several scholars.

Standing taller than any Human, a Werewolf Champion is a formidable opponent; their claws can pierce a breastplate, and they wield even sharper blades. These Champions harbour a ravenous hunger caused by the Curse that pushes them to track their prey relentlessly. It is as if the wildness of the deep forests of the Vampiric Marches had coalesced into one being of primitive fury. Werewolf Champions are pack leaders, those who were able to prove their strength and survive the Vremyasag while also retaining enough of their sanity to prevent the Curse from turning them into mindless beasts.

Gremyir had fought as a Human under Sevrig I during the Havoc Wars, leading his tribe of Volshoboz (Forest people) in ambushes and raids. He had become an expert in irregular warfare, and the Havoc Warriors had nicknamed him the Night Hunter. When the Curse turned him into a Werewolf, Gremyir naturally became the Champion of a pack composed of other former forest peoples. Lady Imruskoza, Marchioness of Telen Valley, was only fourteen years old when the Curse turned her into a Vampire. Her father and brothers had been slain at the battle of the Red Road and she had inherited the family title.

product.description: The sombre elegance and threatening aura of a Vampire Lord mounted on their Undead Steed are unmatched. Whether they are leading the charge, galloping between units to coordinate the ranks, or issuing a challenge to an enemy leader, Vampire Lords are the striking image of their country, a land of fierce warriors changed by a fateful curse. Necromancers create Steeds with the utmost care, as they are considered an extension of their rider. Thanks to their Undead nature, they never tire nor need to feed, except for the occasional piece of flesh found on the battlefield.

gains.name: Winged Terror

product.description: When a Vampire Lord descends from the sky on a Winged Terror, the wise run for cover. These massive beasts can rip a horse’s head clean off and are prone to Curse-induced pangs of hunger that can lead them to swallow a Human whole, while the Vampire rider is a consummate fighter who can control their mount as if it were an extension of themselves. It goes without saying that a Winged Terror is a fear-inducing sight. These Undead monsters are the mounts of choice of Vampire Lords when they want to lead devastating charges on powerful enemy units.

product.description:
The thunderous gallop of a mounted Vampire approaching is a sound that sends chills down the spine of their enemies. But the most experienced know that the most worrying part is when that sound suddenly stops, for it means that they need to stop looking ahead and start looking up into the dark sky.
For millennia, riding a horse has been one of the symbols of the high status enjoyed by the nobles of the Marches. After the Ritual transformed the country and made it difficult to breed quality horses, significant expenses were incurred to develop an Undead steed that could properly serve.

gains.name: Zombie Dragon

product.description: Zombie Dragons are among the largest beasts fielded by the Vampiric Undead. These monsters, the size of a small boat, can obliterate almost anything and have been known to sometimes destroy entire armies by themselves with the aid of their devastating breathing attacks. These creatures of legend are a testament to the terrifying power of necromancy. Dragons have been extinct for centuries. Already rare, they were hunted to extinction by the aristocracy of the Marches, eager to eliminate this threat and earn the prestigious title of Dragon Lord.

gains.name: Skeleton Dragon

product.description: Perhaps the largest, most powerful creatures in the Vampiric Marches, Skeleton Dragons are capable of razing a town to the ground or toppling a castle’s tower. Their arrival is announced by a blood-curdling, high-pitched howl that is produced by the wind whistling through their bones. It is the last sound heard by many who have drawn the ire of the Vampiric Undead. There are only a handful of Skeleton Dragons in the Marches; their creation can take several decades, from assembling the bones to imbuing each part with the many enchantments destined to keep it together.

gains.name: Stitched Zombie Horde

product.description: Emerging from a crypt on a literal wave of bodies, a Vampiric Lord with Stitched Horde is a vision of horror that turns reality into a nightmare. Those who witness such a calamity coming down upon them may utter a prayer, asking that their bodies won't be made to join the ranks of the Undead. A prayer that is, alas, rarely fulfilled. The Stitched Horde is an eccentric strategy that is seen by many Vampires as a bit distasteful since it involves the lowest of the Undead. However, it is an impressive display of power and can evoke feelings of abject terror in mortal foes.

product.description: When mounted on a powerful Undead Steed, a Skeleton Champion becomes a figure of impending doom, appearing as a herald of death to lead legions of the fallen into battle. They are often nobles of the old Western Marches, who died long before the Ritual and were raised afterwards, drawn from their ceremonial tumuli or crypts to fight once again. It is not uncommon for a Vampire to have several Skeleton Champions in his armies that are his own ancestors.

gains.name: Bat Beast

product.description: A Ghoul Champion on a Bat Beast is a powerful fighter who can inflict terrible losses anywhere on the battlefield. Soldiers who witness one gliding above them like death itself will sometimes run away in terror before any fight can occur. Only the strongest, most battle-tested Ghoul Champions can ride such a mount; it is one of the highest honours a Ghoul can receive. A Bat Beast cannot simply be gifted; the Champion must gain the Beast’s trust, bribing it with meat and proving his lack of fear. Any sign of hesitation will typically result in the Ghoul becoming dessert.

gains.name: Bat Dragon

product.description: Bat Dragons were created by Necromancers who simply felt that Giant Bats were not big enough, and hoped to find a way to produce a beast akin to a Dragon without needing to start from an actual draconic corpse. By exposing Giant Bats to extreme amounts of Curse energy and subjecting them to intricate necromantic rituals, they managed to somewhat reach their goals.

Corpse Masters walk to battle wearing raggedy clothes and carrying a gallows-shaped staff from which hang rotting body parts, the material that gave them their name. Wild Curse energy emanates from them, seeming to darken the air around them. With a flick of the wrist, they are able to control the movements of dozens of Stitched Zombies, sending them shambling towards the enemy like grotesque flesh puppets.

Chosen from among the most promising Champions, Skeleton Commanders represent the epitome of their kind. They possess all of the cunning and martial skill they once had in life, combined with the resolute loyalty and unwavering determination imbued by the Necromancer who raised them. Skeleton Commanders are relentless in pursuit of their goals and extremely difficult to truly kill, making them a force to be reckoned with.

specialRules.name: Repel Ambushers
specialRules.description: Enemy units using Ambush must be set up over 12" away from this model's unit.

specialRules.name: Instinctive
specialRules.description: When this model is activated, if it is able to shoot/charge an enemy unit, then it must immediately attack the closest valid target and gets +1 to hit rolls for that attack.

specialRules.name: Infiltrate
specialRules.description: Counts as having Ambush, but may be deployed anywhere over 3" away from enemy unit.

specialRules.name: Teleport
specialRules.description: Once per activation, before attacking, you may place this model anywhere fully within 3" of its position when using Advance/Charge actions, or fully within 6" of its position when using Rush actions.

specialRules.name: Sergeant
specialRules.description: This model gets AP(+1) when attacking.

specialRules.name: Unique Hero
specialRules.description: This hero may only be taken once per party.

specialRules.name: Defense
specialRules.description: This model gets +X to Defense rolls.

specialRules.name: Piercing Marksman
specialRules.description: When shooting at enemies over 9" away, this model's weapons get AP(+1).

specialRules.name: Reanimation
specialRules.description: When a unit where all models have this rule is activated, roll as many dice as the max. number of models/wounds it could restore. For each 5+ you may restore one model/wound. Note that new models may only be restored if they can be placed in coherency with non-restored models.

specialRules.name: Bane when Shooting
specialRules.description: This model gets Bane when shooting.

specialRules.name: Cursed Undead
specialRules.description: When a unit where most models have this rule takes wounds, roll one die for each. On a 6+ it is ignored.

specialRules.name: Enhanced Cursed Undead
specialRules.description: If most models in this unit have Cursed Undead, they ignore wounds on rolls of 5-6 from Cursed Undead (instead of only on 6+).

specialRules.name: Shred in Melee
specialRules.description: This model gets Shred in melee.

specialRules.name: Brace in Melee
specialRules.description: This model gets Brace(1) in melee.

specialRules.name: Spell Resistance
specialRules.description: When a unit where most models have this rule takes wounds, roll one die for each. On a 6+ it is ignored. If the wounds were from a spell, then they are ignored on a 2+ instead.

specialRules.name: Spawn
specialRules.description: Add a friendly AI unit of X to the party, which is deployed as if it were a hero. This unit is activated after all Heroes, and follows the AI activation rules.

specialRules.name: Fragment
specialRules.description: When attacking units where most models have Defense 4+ to Defense 6+, the target must re-roll successful unmodified Defense results of 4-6.

specialRules.name: No Retreat
specialRules.description: When a unit where most models have this rule fails a Morale Test that causes it to be Shaken or Routed, the test counts as passed instead. Then, roll as many dice as the number of wounds it would take to fully destroy it, and for each result of 1-3 the unit takes one wound, which can't be ignored.

specialRules.name: Mind Control
specialRules.description: Only one use per game. Once per activation, before attacking, pick up to 3 enemy units within 18" in line of sight, which must take a Morale Test. If failed you may move it by up to 6" in a straight line in any direction. Units may only be moved once per round in this way.

specialRules.name: Casting Buff
specialRules.description: Once per activation, before attacking, pick one friendly model within 12" with Caster, which gets +1 to casting rolls once (next time the effect would apply).

specialRules.name: Protected
specialRules.description: When a unit where most models have this rule takes wounds, roll one die for each. On a 6+ it is ignored.

specialRules.name: Enhanced Protected
specialRules.description: If most models in this unit have Protected, they ignore wounds on rolls of 5-6 from Protected (instead of only on 6+).

specialRules.name: Ambush
specialRules.description: May be set aside before deployment. At the start of any round after the first, may be placed anywhere over 9” away from enemy units.

specialRules.name: AP
specialRules.description: Targets get -X to Defense rolls when blocking hits.

specialRules.name: Hero
specialRules.description: Units within 6” of friendly Heroes may use the Hero’s Quality for Morale Tests as long as the Hero isn’t Shaken.

specialRules.name: Bane
specialRules.description: Ignores Regeneration, and when attacking, the target must re-roll unmodified Defense results of 6.

specialRules.name: Shred
specialRules.description: For each unmodified result of 1 to block hits, this weapon deals 1 extra wound.

specialRules.name: Brace
specialRules.description: Enemies charging this unit get -X total Impact rolls, unless this unit is Fatigued.

specialRules.name: Caster
specialRules.description: Gets X spell tokens at the start of each round, but can’t have more than 6 at once. Once per activation, before attacking, spend as many tokens as the spell’s value to try casting one or more spells (only one try per spell). Pick a target and roll one die, and on 4+ resolve the spell’s effect. Heroes may spend any number of tokens/power before rolling to get +1 to the roll per token/power, or to give an enemy Caster within 18” -1 to their roll per token/power.

specialRules.name: Deadly
specialRules.description: Assign each wound to one model, and multiply it by X. Hits from Deadly must be resolved first, and these wounds don’t carry over to other models if the original target is killed.
